title: Graceful Spot and Reserved Handoff - PRD Concept
body:
Purpose / problem we see
- Customers want lower unit cost by using spare/spot GPUs for transient burst traffic but also need predictable, SLA-backed capacity.
- Spot reclamation currently causes abrupt failures or long cold-restarts for some tenants. Existing fallbacks (immediate failover to hosted models or throttling) either increase cost or break latency SLOs.
- We need a composable way for tenants and ops to define how to gracefully hand off workloads between opportunistic spot resources and reserved (committed) capacity with clear economic and isolation properties.

Objectives (what success looks like)
- Provide a customer-configurable handoff policy that preserves latency SLOs for high-priority requests while minimizing incremental cost.
- Auto-migrate active KV-cached sessions from spot back to reserved resources with <500ms extra tail latency for warm sessions where feasible.
- Offer transparent billing/ledgering for spot-burst usage vs reserved consumption (line-itemized).
- Provide operator tooling for isolation checks and safe preemption windows to avoid noisy-neighbor escalations.

Non-goals
- Replacing entire autoscaler — this is an edge for burst/spot integration, not a full rewrite.
- Solving model correctness or prompt-level quality regressions across variants.

Design overview (core idea)
- Introduce a "handoff layer" in the serving stack that sits between request router and pool allocator. The layer tracks per-tenant session affinity, KV-cache residency, and active request shapes.
- Two primary resource classes: SPOT (opportunistic, low-cost) and RESERVED (committed, SLA-backed). Tenants may have both.
- Handoff policy is expressed per-tenant (or per-route) as a small DSL: {priority, margin_pct, preempt_horizon_ms, migration_mode}.
  - priority = high|normal|background (maps to preemption tolerance)
  - margin_pct = fraction of reserved headroom to keep free before triggering proactive migration (e.g., 10%)
  - preempt_horizon_ms = time to allow graceful migration after reclaim signal (e.g., 5000ms)
  - migration_mode = warm-migrate | queuify | failover
- When spot reclamation events occur (from infra), handoff layer consults policy and decides: (A) warm-migrate active sessions/kvcache to reserved hosts; (B) enqueue new requests until reserved capacity available; (C) let low-priority requests fail/redirect.

Autoscaling integration
- Use a hybrid autoscaler: reactive (instant scale-up of reserved pool where tenant has budget/credit) + predictive (model-based forecast from recent traffic spikes and billing patterns).
- Autoscaler exposes an API for the handoff layer to request immediate reserved slices: request_reserved(tenant, cores, gpus, ttl_ms, priority_hint).
- Reserved allocation honors tenant limits and grace credits; operator-configurable escalation policy when limits are reached (soft-decline, overcommit with billing alert, or reject).

Isolation controls and safety fences
- Tenant-level isolation score computed from: noisy-neighbor history, concurrency, memory footprint, and accelerator contention. High-risk tenants get conservative margin_pct defaults.
- Soft-eviction window: when reserved cannot absorb migrated sessions, system applies staged degradation: first reduce batching size or precision (quantization profile), next reduce throughput cap, last apply request shedding for background priority.
- Operator features: per-pool quarantine and manual drain triggers, ability to pin sessions to reserved only, and automated post-mortem markers to track reclaim impact.

Billing / ledgering model
- Two-part metric export: burst_spot_seconds and burst_spot_tokens (tokens processed on spot GPUs), and migration_cost_tokens for operations during warm-migrate.
- Provide line-item in tenant billing showing spot savings and reserved delta, plus credits consumed (if using burst credits).

APIs and tenant controls (sketch)
- HandOffPolicy (route-level config)
  - "policy_name": string
  - "priority": "high|normal|background"
  - "margin_pct": integer
  - "preempt_horizon_ms": integer
  - "migration_mode": "warm-migrate|queuify|failover"
  - "burst_credits": integer (optional)
- Tenant-level: enable_spot_burst: boolean, max_spot_fraction: 0-100
- SDK: redwood.dedicated.set_handoff_policy(tenant_id, policy)

Operational concerns / telemetry
- New metrics: handoff_events_total, handoff_success_rate, migrate_duration_ms p50/p95/p99, spot_reclaim_events, queued_requests_during_handoff, reserved_scale_requests, reserved_scale_failures.
- Traces should include reclaim signal -> handoff decision -> migration steps -> final state. Tag traces with tenant_id and route.
- Alerts: handoff_success_rate < 95% for >5m for high-priority tenants; reserved_scale_failures rate > 1% for 10m.

Runbook (operator sketch)
- Reclaim detected -> auto-handoff attempts logged. If handoff_success_rate low, run quick checks:
  1) Are reserved pools healthy? (pool_liveness, nvlink errors)
  2) Are migration failures due to KV serialization errors? Check logs for kvcache evictions.
  3) If reserved allocation failed: escalate quota with ops-runbook link, temporarily switch tenant to queuify or reduce margin.
- Manual opt-out: teams can set migration_mode=failover to avoid warm state moves if they prefer cost predictability.

Risks and mitigations
- Warm-migrate complexity: migrating large KV caches can be expensive and may nullify cost savings. Mitigate: limit kvcache size for spot sessions or do incremental replication.
- Billing confusion: customers might not understand micro-billing from many small migrations. Mitigate: provide summarized monthly ledger and explain in console.
- Attack surface: lower-priority tenants might be used to trigger reclaim for noisy neighbors. Mitigate: isolation scoring and throttling and require attestation for cross-tenant bursts.

Open questions / decisions needed
- Default margin_pct by priority bucket? (ops suggested default 12% for high, 6% normal, 2% background)
- Migration semantics for long-running chat sessions that have huge KV caches — limit or require pinned reserved for those tenants?
- Billing model for failed migrations (who pays for migration cost if reserved allocate fails mid-migrate?)

Next steps / immediate action items
- Prototype: small internal canary for 10 tenants using warm-migrate with TTL-based kvcache replication (owner: Liam). (2 sprints)
- Instrumentation: add handoff metrics and traces (owner: Rosa). (1 sprint)
- Billing: design ledger rows and UI mock for console (owner: Maya). (1 sprint)
- Run a chaos experiment: simulate spot reclaim patterns and verify handoff success and SLO impact (owner: Devon). (after prototype)

Notes to self / rough thoughts
- Consider combining warm-migrate with progressive quantization: step down precision to shrink kvcache before migrating.
- Might be worth a "handoff simulator" locally: replay reclaim traces against candidate policies.

References / links
- Confluence design sketch: https://confluence.redwood/DEDICATED/graceful-handoff-arch
- JIRA: JIRA-DED-1423 (handoff prototype epic)
- GH PR: github.com/redwood-inference/dedicated-autoscaler/pull/78

This is intentionally a concept-level PRD and ops playbook. Looking for feedback on the migration_mode semantics, sensible defaults for margin_pct, and which tenants should be eligible for spot-backed bursts by default.
